candidates.title: PRT player restarts from an unsynced backup clone (machine.revert) chosen by a content rehash, then uses its unrebuilt cached hash tree, discarding the guaranteed epoch machine
candidates.role: Support (the PRT player in doc/recipes, per the AUDIT.md table); it stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua: stored_machine_pair_methods:commit (lines ~1137-1150: remove machine.revert, clone_stored(machine, machine.revert), sync_stored(machine.revert)); revert_interrupted_input (lines ~2864-2880, branch 1: get_stored_root_hash(backup) == root_hash -> remove the synced machine, clone the backup into machine, no sync); get_stored_root_hash (~2850-2861, loads with clear_hash_tree=true only for the comparison); reopen_epoch_directory (~3076-3102: new_stored_machine(root_hash, machine_directory) loads the clone with SHARING_ALL and WITHOUT clear_hash_tree); run_next_input (~2265-2270: commit_epoch_state writes state.json at boundary N before pair:commit replaces the backup).
candidates.description: pair:commit() writes the backup directly under its final name: it removes the old machine.revert, clones the (destroyed and synced) epoch machine into machine.revert and only then syncs it. Unlike the CLI stored revert mode and run-rolling-calculator-from-storage.lua (clone to .revert.tmp, sync, rename), a machine.revert that exists is therefore not always a synced copy. state.json already records boundary N when this happens (commit_epoch_state runs first). On restart, revert_interrupted_input picks the backup whenever its CONTENT hash, recomputed with clear_hash_tree, equals state.json's root hash; it then removes the epoch machine directory (which is O2-guaranteed: destroyed and synced at boundary N) and clones the backup over it, without syncing. reopen_epoch_directory then loads that clone with SHARING_ALL and without clear_hash_tree, so the clone's cached hash-tree data (.dht/.dpt/hash_tree.sht/hash_tree.phtc), which after a power loss before the sync is in an unspecified state, is trusted. The rehash check covers only the contents; the code comment on get_stored_root_hash itself says 'after a power loss its cached hash tree may not match its contents'. If the cached data is damaged, the load either fails the root-hash assert (the player cannot reopen) or passes it and later reports root hashes that are not the content hash (wrong computation-hash leaves, wrong claims).
candidates.trigger: Host crash or power loss (O2 lists power loss as a stop) of the honest player's host after pair:commit() has cloned the epoch machine into machine.revert and before sync_stored(machine.revert) returns, i.e. right after any input is recorded; then the supervisor relaunches the player. No adversary action is needed, but an adversary sending many inputs widens the exposure (one window per input).
candidates.reachability: Reachable on the player's normal path: the window exists once per input (and at the epoch's first commit). Whether a crash leaves contents durable while cached hash-tree files are partial depends on the filesystem: with the copy fallback of clone_file (ext4 or any filesystem without FICLONE, which the manual supports: 'writable ones use reference links on copy-on-write filesystems') writeback of delalloc data is not ordered across or within files, so config.json and the data files can be durable while the tail of a .dht or the .phtc payloads are holes. On XFS reflink the remap transactions are logged in order, which makes a partial clone less likely but O2 still gives no guarantee for an unsynced directory. Regardless of filesystem, the player violates O2 by construction: it resumes from a directory it was writing when it stopped while a guaranteed one exists.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The excluded case is 'Defects that need the honest operator to reload a stored directory that O2 does not guarantee, such as one being written ... when its process stopped'. Here the defect IS the operator implementation choosing that directory; the guaranteed directory (epoch machine, 'synced after the last change to its contents and ... destroyed without a crash before that sync') exists and is deleted. Section 5: 'O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them'. O2: 'A process that stops (crash, kill, or power loss) leaves every stored directory it was writing or sharing in an unspecified state. The operator discards those directories and resumes from a guaranteed one'. So not out of scope. 2. Role: the PRT player is Support per AUDIT.md ('No production deployment runs the player'); section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3. High/Medium cases: as honest operator it would be Critical (step 4), so as support it is Medium by the quoted clause. 4. Critical (for the role it stands in for): violates O2 and R4 ('After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim') on the honest operator's path ('Restarting after a stop (O2)'); the outcome is a completeness failure ('The honest operator computes a wrong hash ... or cannot respond in time'). 5. n/a. Claimed: Medium (support), would be Critical in an honest-operator implementation.
candidates.threat_to_goal: If a production node copied this restart logic, one badly timed power loss would make the honest operator either unable to reopen its epoch (assert 'stored machine hash mismatch', no further claims or moves, the honest claim times out) or, worse, silently compute root hashes that are not the content hashes, so it commits to a wrong mcycle computation hash and loses every match. Either way a dishonest claim can win (completeness failure, section 1).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/O2/exp1.lua and exp2.lua with the in-tree build (bugs/env.sh) on the baremetal-template config. Setup mirrors the player: A = clone of the template, loaded with SHARING_ALL, get_root_hash, destroyed, synced (the epoch machine at boundary N); B = clone_stored(A) (the backup), then a span of B's RAM .dht is zeroed to model writeback lost before the sync. exp2 with leaves of pages 0..63 zeroed printed: selector_ok=true (B rehashed with clear_hash_tree equals the reference root, so revert_interrupted_input would pick B), load_assert_ok=true (B loaded with SHARING_ALL and no clear reports the reference root, so new_stored_machine's assert passes), then after delivering one input with revert root = reference root and running to the next yield: A reports 0xa460a4beae96dee0..., B reports 0x2e03b6f2bd40a9f8... while B's contents rehashed give 0xa460a4beae96dee0... (silent wrong hash). Zeroing the whole RAM .dht or its second half makes the no-clear load report a different root (assert fails: the player cannot reopen).
candidates.test_idea: Lua test with prt.lua's stored player helpers (or a copy of revert_interrupted_input + new_stored_machine): build an epoch directory with state.json at boundary N, a synced epoch machine, and a machine.revert produced by clone_stored without sync whose RAM .dht has a zeroed span (modelling the power loss). Call the reopen path, deliver the next input and run it, and assert that the reported root hash equals the content hash recomputed with clear_hash_tree (or that the player reopened from the synced epoch machine / rebuilt the hash tree). Exits 1 today; 0 once commit uses clone-to-tmp+sync+rename (so an existing machine.revert is always synced) or reopen loads with clear_hash_tree / syncs and verifies.

candidates.title: Reopening a sealed epoch replaces the synced epoch machine with an unsynced clone and then deletes the only synced copy, so a power loss after the restart blocks every later reopen
candidates.role: Support (PRT player); stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua: reopen_epoch_directory (~3065-3125): revert_interrupted_input(directory, root_hash) then, for a sealed epoch, remove_leftover_stored_machine(machine.revert); revert_interrupted_input branch 1 (~2867-2872): remove machine, clone_stored(machine.revert, machine) without sync_stored; seal_epoch_state (~2722-2738): state.json sealed before machine.revert is removed; branch 2 assert 'the epoch machine does not match its state' (~2874).
candidates.description: seal_epoch_state destroys and syncs the epoch machine, commits the sealed state.json, and only then removes machine.revert. If the player stops between those last two steps, the next reopen runs revert_interrupted_input: machine.revert (synced, holding the final state) matches, so the synced epoch machine is deleted and replaced by an UNSYNCED clone of the backup; reopen_epoch_directory then removes machine.revert (durably: remove_stored syncs the parent). From that moment the epoch directory holds no O2-guaranteed copy of the machine. If the host loses power before writeback of the clone, the next reopen finds no backup, takes branch 2, loads the partial epoch machine and hits assert(get_stored_root_hash(machine_directory) == root_hash), so the player cannot reopen the sealed epoch whose dispute it must defend. The epoch machine is not otherwise needed for a sealed epoch (units use the cache entries), which makes the failure gratuitous.
candidates.trigger: Two host events: a stop of the honest player between the sealed state.json commit and the removal of machine.revert (any crash or kill), then a host crash or power loss shortly after the relaunch, before the kernel writes back the clone made by revert_interrupted_input.
candidates.reachability: Reachable without any adversary input, but needs a stop in a narrow window followed by a power loss within the writeback interval; on filesystems where the clone is a copy (no FICLONE) the clone's data can be lost while its directory entries are durable (the parent sync done by remove_stored of machine.revert persists the metadata).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Not out of scope: the defect is the operator implementation leaving no guaranteed directory and then requiring an unguaranteed one; O2: 'The operator discards those directories and resumes from a guaranteed one'; section 5: 'The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them'. 2. Role: Support (AUDIT.md: PRT player). 3. Section 3: support defect that 'would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator' -> Medium. 4. In the honest-operator role it violates R4 ('After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim'): the operator cannot respond in time (completeness failure) -> Critical there. 5. n/a. Claimed Medium.
candidates.threat_to_goal: The honest player stops being able to reopen a sealed epoch in dispute, so its claim times out and a dishonest claim can win (completeness failure).
candidates.evidence: Code reading only (same mechanism as candidate 1: revert_interrupted_input branch 1 clones without syncing, and the sealed path deletes the backup right after). Not run.
candidates.test_idea: Build a sealed epoch directory with state.json sealed, a synced epoch machine and a synced machine.revert holding the final state. Run reopen_epoch_directory, then simulate the lost writeback by truncating (to holes) a data file of the new epoch machine and restoring nothing else, and reopen again: the test asserts the second reopen succeeds (or that after the first reopen the epoch machine directory had been synced / the guaranteed copy kept). Exits 1 today.

candidates.title: collect_mcycle_root_hashes loses page dirty marks held only in its context when the interpreter throws (e.g. allocation failure), leaving the hash tree, and a later synced shared directory, inconsistent with the contents
candidates.component: Hash collection (collect_mcycle_root_hashes) and its state access
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp collect_mcycle_root_hashes (~2486-2520): try { interpret_with_console(a, ...) } catch only machine_console_exception; context.dirty_pages are marked into the dirty page trees only after interpret returns. src/collect-mcycle-hashes-state-access.hpp do_write_memory_word/mark_dirty_word (~77-82, 464-466): every memory write is recorded only in context.dirty_pages (an ankerl::unordered_dense::set, reserved to at most 4096 entries); page-table A/D updates (translate-virtual-address.hpp:77 a.write_memory_word) are not covered by the write TLB, so the context is their only record.
candidates.description: During collection, writes that do not go through the write TLB (notably PTE accessed/dirty updates on page-table pages) are recorded only in context.dirty_pages. Any exception other than machine_console_exception escaping interpret_with_console (for instance std::bad_alloc from dirty_pages.insert growing past its reservation, or from another allocation) unwinds out of collect_mcycle_root_hashes without marking those pages in the dirty page trees. The page contents were changed, their .dht leaves were not, and no dirty mark remains, so every later update_hash_tree in that process skips them: get_root_hash, proofs and later collections return hashes that are not the content hash. With SHARING_ALL, destroy (which marks only the write TLB pages) plus sync_stored produces a directory that O2 guarantees but whose cached hash tree disagrees with its contents, so it loads as a different root hash. R9 explicitly covers 'updates that fail inside a running process, which then keeps using the machine'.
candidates.trigger: A host fault (allocation failure under a memory limit such as RLIMIT_AS, or any other exception thrown inside interpret) during collect_mcycle_root_hashes called by a node that keeps the machine (the JSON-RPC server keeps it after returning the error) or destroys and syncs its shared directory. The guest controls how many pages it dirties per period (more than 4096 forces the set to grow).
candidates.reachability: The exception path is reachable whenever an allocation inside the interpreter loop fails; with Linux overcommit plain malloc rarely fails, so it mostly needs an address-space or allocator limit. Not demonstrated; a prover could inject the failure with an LD_PRELOAD malloc shim or RLIMIT_AS.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? 'Host faults, such as a full disk, as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state' - this turns a host fault into a wrong hash, so it stays in scope. 2. Role: collect_mcycle_root_hashes is Honest operator (AUDIT.md table). 3. No High/Medium case fits (the state is reachable: any guest using virtual memory updates PTE A/D bits). 4. Critical: violates R9 ('This applies to every cached, incremental, or persisted hash, after any sequence of documented operations. It includes interrupted or failed updates') and section 4 ('the emulator must never turn one into a wrong hash'). If triage reads 'bad_alloc' as not a realistic host fault, it falls to Low. Claimed Critical with that caveat.
candidates.threat_to_goal: A node that survives the failed collection (or reloads a shared directory it destroyed and synced) computes state hashes that do not match the contents, so it commits to wrong claims or proofs that do not verify (completeness failure).
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: catch block catches only machine_console_exception; dirty marks applied after interpret; write_verified_tlb marks evicted write-TLB pages directly, so only non-TLB writes (PTE updates) depend solely on the context. Not run.
candidates.test_idea: Run collect_mcycle_root_hashes on a Linux machine with a malloc shim that fails the Nth allocation after collection starts (or a tiny RLIMIT_AS margin), catch the error, then compare machine:get_root_hash() with the root of the same machine reloaded/rebuilt with clear_hash_tree (or verify_hash_tree): assert they are equal. Fails today if PTE pages were dirtied in the interrupted period.

not_covered: Crash-consistency of reflink/hard-link clones on specific filesystems (XFS, btrfs, APFS) was reasoned about, not tested with real power-loss injection (dm-log-writes or similar).
fsync error semantics (a failed fsync followed by a retried sync_stored that succeeds while data was dropped) and their handling by callers.
Windows and macOS persistence paths (FlushFileBuffers, F_FULLFSYNC, clonefile, no unified page cache warning).
JSON-RPC server side of store/load/clone/sync/rename/remove (remote paths, fork_server snapshots and rebind) and the forked (non-stored) player.
store() with CM_SHARING_CONFIG/NONE (copying initial backing stores with their dht/dpt while sht/phtc come from the running machine): only partially reasoned, judged consistent, not tested.

hash_tree::update failure path: m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages is not persisted, so a failed update followed by destroy+sync+reload would mark pages clean without bubbling; I found no reachable failure of update() (only logic errors/bad_alloc), so not reported.
collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes / update_words interaction with persisted dirty page trees and the page cache under exceptions (uarch traps, reset_dirty_words growth).
replace_memory_range and its effect on stored directories; the CLI's --store/%h and --load clone:/sharing/sync combinations beyond the stored revert mode.

PRT player: machine cache entries, agreed pair, checkpoint rename and remove_epoch_files were read and looked O2-compliant; the player-restart harness (bugs/harness/player-restart) was not run (long, shared chain).
Partial phtc corruption effects (cache entries whose page copy and hash tree disagree with an 'initialized' tag) were not tested separately from the dht case.
